title: Employee Training Tracking: 5 Methods + Best Tools (2026)
summary: Employee training tracking made simple: compare 5 methods, see the best tools for small teams, and learn how to track certifications before they expire.
body_markdown:
Employee training tracking is how you document what your team has completed and when each certification expires. Training tracking covers onboarding, compliance training, certifications like food handler cards, and role-specific skills. Done well, you can answer “Who’s current on food safety?” in seconds instead of after an hour of digging through folders.


For small businesses with hourly teams, the stakes show up on inspection day or the week a certification quietly lapses. This guide covers five ways to handle employee training tracking, what records to keep, how to choose a tool, and how Homebase handles certifications.


## **Employee Training Tracking in Short**


The best way to track employee training is one record per person: what they completed, when, when it expires, and proof. Then pick the method that fits your team.


- **Small team, simple needs:** A spreadsheet works if someone checks it on a set schedule.
- **Growing team or more locations:** Move certifications into an app with employee profiles, so expiration dates live in one place.
- **Building your own courses:** Use a learning management system (LMS).
- **Hourly teams on the move:** Choose a tool your team can use from a phone.


## **What Is Employee Training Tracking?**


[Employee training](https://www.joinhomebase.com/hiring-and-onboarding/employee-training) tracking is the process of documenting, monitoring, and managing training activities, certifications, and[compliance requirements](https://www.joinhomebase.com/hr-compliance/labor-law-compliance) . Tracking helps you answer questions like “Who completed food safety training?” and “Whose CPR certification expires next month?”


Training records, course completions, and certifications aren’t the same thing, so it helps to track them separately:


- **Training records:** What an employee was taught and when, such as onboarding or opening procedures.
- **Course completion:** Whether an employee finished a required course.
- **Certifications:** Credentials issued by an outside authority, like a[ServSafe food handler card](https://www.joinhomebase.com/hr-compliance/workplace-safety) , an alcohol service license, or an American Red Cross CPR certificate.
- **Renewal tracking:** The expiration dates that keep a certification current.


A clear plan for[training new employees](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-train-new-employees) makes records easier to keep, since every course and certification you assign becomes something to track.


## **Why Does Employee Training Tracking Matter for Small Businesses?**


### **Legal Compliance and Avoiding Fines**


Many OSHA standards require employers to train employees. The maximum penalty is $16,550 per serious violation and $165,514 for willful or repeated ones, according to[OSHA’s 2026 penalty adjustments](https://www.osha.gov/memos/2026-05-21/2026-annual-adjustments-osha-civil-penalties) . Those are maximums, not automatic fines for a missing record, and which training applies depends on your industry.


Food safety and alcohol service rules vary even more. States and local health departments set their own food handler and manager certification requirements, often using the[FDA’s 2026 Food Code](https://www.fda.gov/food/fda-food-code/food-code-2026) as a model. Alcohol server training and renewal periods differ by state, so check what your authorities require, then track those credentials.


### **Audit Readiness**


Inspectors and auditors may ask for proof that employees are trained or certified. When certifications and expiration dates sit in one place, you can pull records quickly.


## **What Challenges Come With Employee Training Tracking?**


- **Losing track of who’s trained on what:** Paper certificates get lost, and expiration dates go unrecorded.
- **Recertifications slipping:** Renewal periods vary by credential and state, and without one record, something gets missed.
- **No central record when someone leaves:** When a manager quits, their knowledge of who completed what leaves too.
- **Poor visibility across locations:** Corporate can’t pull a company-wide report without calling every store.


## **How to Track Employee Training: 5 Practical Methods**


Match your method to your team size, budget, and training requirements. Here are five approaches, from simplest to most sophisticated.


### **Spreadsheets for Employee Training Tracking**


Best for small teams with simple needs. Create columns for employee name, training type, completion date, expiration date, and where proof is stored.


For employee training tracking, spreadsheets are free, but nothing alerts you when a certification is about to expire. You’ve outgrown a spreadsheet when updating it takes hours each week, or when you schedule someone for a shift they weren’t certified for.


### **LMS Tools for Employee Training Tracking**


Best for businesses creating their own training courses, not just tracking completion. A learning management system like TalentLMS lets you build courses with quizzes, host videos, and track who finished what.


Most small businesses with hourly teams don’t need this. LMS plans are priced by user count and offer more than you need if you only track outside certifications like food safety or CPR.


### **HR Tools for Employee Training Tracking**


Best for small businesses that want certifications stored with the rest of their team records. These tools keep certifications and expiration dates on each employee’s profile. Some, like Homebase, also include[scheduling](https://www.joinhomebase.com/employee-scheduling) , time tracking, and[payroll](https://www.joinhomebase.com/payroll/online-payroll) in the same app.


The advantage is one app for schedules, payroll, and certification records, instead of signing in to three different systems every day.


### **Standalone Certification Trackers**


Best for businesses focused on credentials and compliance documents. These tools store certificates, track expiration dates, and generate audit reports, but they don’t connect to your scheduling or payroll tools, so you manage training in one place and shifts in another.


### **Mobile Apps for Hourly Teams**


Best for deskless team members who don’t sit at a computer. Mobile apps let employees view their own records and attach photos of their certificates, so a new food handler card goes into their profile the same day.


## **How Do You Choose an Employee Training Tracking Tool?**


Whichever tool you consider, ask these questions:


- Can employees add certifications from their phones?
- Does the tool store expiration dates and send alerts? If so, who gets them and when?
- Can managers see every certification and expiration date in one report?
- Does the tool connect to scheduling and payroll, or do you manage those elsewhere?


One caution: a tracking tool records what you enter, so you’re still responsible for verifying that each credential is valid and meets your state and local requirements.

### **1. Connecteam**


**Best for:** Deskless teams that run everything from phones.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/connecteam/reviews) 4.6/5 (3,505 reviews) ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/153140/Connecteam/reviews/) 4.6/5 (5,318 reviews)


**What it is:** Connecteam is a mobile-first app with three separately priced hubs: Operations for time clocks and scheduling, Communications for chat and updates, and HR and Skills for courses, quizzes, and documents. It suits deskless teams that work from phones, and its Expert plan adds document expiration dates with a notice before they expire.


**What’s included:**


- GPS time clock and job scheduling in the Operations hub.
- Courses, quizzes, and documents in the HR and Skills hub.
- Document expiration dates with a notice before expiry, starting on the Expert plan.


**Pricing:** Free for up to 10 users. Paid plans start at $29 a month billed annually for the first 30 users, per hub. Expert is $99 a month billed annually.


**What users like:** A[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/connecteam/) writes, “The app makes managing schedules, breaks, and hours worked effortless.”


**What users criticize:** G2 reviewers most often say useful options need a higher plan or extra cost (229 reviews). One[Capterra reviewer](https://www.capterra.com/p/153140/Connecteam/reviews/) wrote that the desktop version “has been running very slow recently and crashing.”


**Our take:** Connecteam is the closest fit for phone-first teams that need expiry notices on documents. The tradeoff is cost: expiration dates sit on the Expert plan and each hub is priced separately, so the $29 headline understates a full setup.


### **2. TalentLMS**


**Best for:** Businesses that build their own training courses.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/talentlms/reviews) 4.6/5 (805 reviews) ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/132935/TalentLMS/reviews/) 4.7/5 (596 reviews)


**What it is:** TalentLMS is a learning management system for building your own courses, with quizzes, video, and completion reports. It works best when you create training in-house rather than track credentials issued elsewhere. A free plan covers five users and 10 courses.


**What’s included:**


- Course creation with quizzes and video.
- Completion reporting by employee and course.
- A free plan for five users and 10 courses.


**Pricing:** Free for up to five users. Core is $119 a month billed annually ($149 billed monthly) for up to 40 users, priced by users who sign in each month.


**What users like:** A[G2 reviewer](https://g2.com/survey_responses/talentlms-review-8078252) writes, “The pre-built reporting features are fantastic.”


**What users criticize:** G2 reviewers most often cite limited features (38 reviews). A[Capterra reviewer](https://www.capterra.com/p/132935/TalentLMS/reviews/) wrote, “Customization and reporting are somewhat limited, and there are occasional minor bugs.”


**Our take:** TalentLMS makes sense when you write your own training. It records what happens inside its courses, so if your team mostly holds outside credentials like food handler cards, check how it logs those first. Scheduling lives elsewhere.


### **3. BambooHR**


**Best for:** Teams that want a full HR system.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/bamboohr/reviews) 4.4/5 (5,783 reviews) ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/110968/BambooHR/reviews/) 4.6/5 (3,653 reviews)


**What it is:** BambooHR is a full HR system covering hiring, onboarding, time off, benefits, and reporting, with performance management and compliance training courses on higher plans. It fits companies that want one HR record per employee, and per-employee pricing means cost rises with headcount.


**What’s included:**


- HR data and reporting.
- Hiring, onboarding, time off, and benefits tracking.
- Performance management and compliance training courses on higher plans.


**Pricing:** No free tier. Core is $10, Pro is $17, and Elite is $25 per employee a month for companies with more than 25 employees. Teams of 25 or fewer pay a flat monthly rate.


**What users like:** A[G2 reviewer](https://g2.com/products/bamboohr/reviews_and_filters?page=9) calls the interface “the cleanest I’ve seen on an HR portal.”


**What users criticize:** G2 reviewers most often cite limited features (320 reviews), such as holiday management and reporting. One[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/BambooHR/reviews) wrote that “some features feel limited or could be more flexible.”


**Our take:** BambooHR makes sense when HR is already a priority. For hourly teams, it can mean paying per employee for hiring, benefits, and performance tools you won’t use, and G2 lists about two months to implement.


### **4. Trainual**


**Best for:** Teams that want written procedures and training paths.


**Rating:**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/trainual/reviews) 4.7/5 (1,034 reviews) ·[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/175749/Trainual/reviews/) 4.8/5 (510 reviews)


**What it is:** Trainual is a training and documentation app for writing down how your business runs, from opening checklists to equipment protocols. It adds onboarding workflows, role-based assignments, and completion reporting. It publishes no plan prices, so you book a demo for a quote.


**What’s included:**


- Step-by-step process documentation.
- Onboarding workflows and role-based training assignments.
- Training and completion tracking with reporting.


**Pricing:** No free tier. Plans are Core, Pro, Premium, and Enterprise.


**What users like:** A[G2 reviewer](https://g2.com/products/trainual/reviews?page=10) writes that it is “easy and fun to use,” and praises reporting that shows each employee’s progress.


**What users criticize:** G2 reviewers want more flexible customization (52 reviews). One[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/survey_responses/trainual-review-1238459) said “the assigning of courses to users could be improved,” while calling it a picky complaint.


**Our take:** Trainual is strong at documenting how work gets done. The tools we reviewed center on training completion, not expiring credentials, so confirm how it handles renewal dates if that is your main need.


## **How Do You Track Employee Certifications in Homebase?**


Managers and employees can both add certifications to a profile. Here’s how to add one as a manager.


### **How Do Managers Add a Certification?**


1. Sign in to your Homebase account on the web.
2. Select **Team** , then **Roster** .
3. Select an employee’s name to open their profile.
4. Under the **Information** tab, select **+Add a Certificate** .
5. Enter the certificate name and expiration date. You can add an image of the certificate too.
6. Select **Save Changes** .


Use the pencil icon to edit a certification later, or the trash icon to delete it.


### **How Do Employees Add Their Own Certifications?**


On mobile, employees tap **More** on iPhone or the menu icon on Android, then **Profile** , then scroll to **Certificates** . They tap **Add** , enter the name and expiration date, attach a photo if they’d like, and tap **Add** again.


On the web, employees select **Settings** , then **Profile** under **Account** , then **Add New Certificate** . They select **Save Changes** when they’re done.


### **How Do You Review Every Certification in One Place?**


1. Sign in to Homebase on the web.
2. Select **Operations** in the left menu, then **Reports** .
3. Select **Certifications** .
4. Review employee certifications and expiration dates, and follow up with anyone who needs to renew.


Reports open on the web, not in the mobile app, and you can view them for any or all of your locations.


### **When Does Homebase Alert You About Expiring Certifications?**


Homebase can alert you 10 days before an employee’s certification expires.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What Is Employee Training Tracking Software?**


Employee training tracking software is a tool that helps businesses record employee training, certifications, and expiration dates in one place. Most include a central database, mobile access for employees, and reports for audits. Some also send expiration alerts, so check how each tool handles them.


### **Can I Use Excel to Track Employee Training?**


Yes, Excel works for small teams with simple training requirements. Nothing alerts you to upcoming expirations, though, and multiple versions pile up. Move to an app when updating takes hours each week.


### **What Records Should You Keep for Employee Training?**


Keep the employee’s name and title, the certification name, the issuing organization, the completion and expiration dates, and a copy of the certificate. Retention periods depend on the regulation and the credential, so check the rule that applies to yours.


## **Stop Chasing Down Expired Certifications**


Employee training tracking shouldn’t mean digging through filing cabinets during an inspection. The right tool keeps every certification and expiration date in one place and gives your team mobile access to add their own.
